item.title: [LU-20595] lnetconfig: audit cYAML_get_object_item() callers for sibling-recursion matches
item.description:
cYAML_get_object_item() searches recursively. It walks into the children of
the parent node, then into the parent's siblings through cy_next. A caller
that wants only a match under one parent can get a match from a later
sibling instead.

LU-20479 fixed one instance of this shape in cYAML_build_error(). Gerrit
review on change 67235 found a second instance during the fix.

handle_yaml_config_ni() in lnet/utils/lnetconfig/liblnetconfig.c walks a
sequence of local NI entries:

while (cYAML_get_next_seq_item(local_nis, &local_ni) != NULL) {
intf = cYAML_get_object_item(local_ni, "interfaces");
if (intf == NULL)
continue;

A parsed sequence item has cy_string set to NULL. When one local NI entry
has no "interfaces" key, the recursive search does not stop at that entry.
It falls through to the next sibling entry and returns that entry's
"interfaces" node instead. The "continue" statement only fires on the last
entry in the sequence, because only the last entry has no following
sibling to fall through to.

Audit the other cYAML_get_object_item() callers that predate commit
c906ab9c88ef ("LU-7734 lnet: configuration fixes") for the same hazard.
For each caller, confirm the recursive search is safe in that context.
If it is not safe, replace the call with cYAML_get_object_child(), which
searches only the given parent's direct children.

status.description: The issue is open and ready for the assignee to start work on it.

comments.comment:
hornc

Hi, Chris. 

There are too many callers, so I let AI scan the master branch, and got the report above. 

Currently 136 caller are found, and all of them are flat search, 0 is recursive intention.

I don't think there exists any scenario need a search whose intention is beyond current node.

Also I read the commit which introduce the problem.

 

Author: Amir Shehata <ashehata@whamcloud.com>
Date:   Fri Jun 17 15:55:13 2016 -0700
    LU-7734 lnet: configuration fixes
    Fix cpt configuration from DLC to configure the proper list
    of cpts in LNet. Check in LNet that no CPTs are outside the
    available CPTs in the system.
    Fix peer_rtr_credits name to peer_tx_credits to reflect the
    actual value.
    Signed-off-by: Amir Shehata <amir.shehata@intel.com>
    Change-Id: Ic4a3985a470ed901be6166df4079205677921817
    Reviewed-on: http://review.whamcloud.com/20862
    Tested-by: Jenkins

 

with the code

diff --git a/lnet/utils/cyaml/cyaml.c b/lnet/utils/cyaml/cyaml.c
index a713566ba5..de8804bd5c 100644
— a/lnet/utils/cyaml/cyaml.c
+++ b/lnet/utils/cyaml/cyaml.c
@@ -687,19 +687,23 @@ static bool find_obj_iter(struct cYAML *node, void *usr_data, void **out)
 struct cYAML *cYAML_get_object_item(struct cYAML *parent, const char *name)
 {

      struct cYAML *node;
+       struct cYAML *node = parent, *found = NULL;         if (parent == NULL || parent->cy_child == NULL || name == NULL)
+       if (!node || !name)
                return NULL;         node = parent->cy_child;
-       while (node != NULL &&               strcmp(node->cy_string, name) != 0) {               node = node->cy_next;
+       if (node->cy_string) { +               if (strcmp(node->cy_string, name) == 0) +                       return node;         }         return node;
+       if (node->cy_child)
+               found = cYAML_get_object_item(node->cy_child, name);
+
+       if (!found && node->cy_next)
+               found = cYAML_get_object_item(node->cy_next, name);
+
+       return found;
 }
 

It seems the change has nothing to do with the patch's  original purpose. 

So I think it should be safe to just replace "cYAML_get_object_item()" with "cYAML_get_object_child()",

Or revert the change of commit c906ab9c88ef ("LU-7734 lnet: configuration fixes")?
